app.name: Teach Us to Pray
app.description: Learn to pray in your own words, following the pattern Jesus gave in the Lord's Prayer.

intro: There are seven short steps. Each one shows the words of Jesus and asks you one question at a time.
Answer each question as if you are speaking to him, in a sentence of your own. You may leave any question blank.
At the end you will read your prayer through, then pray it out loud.
guide.hint: Write it as you would say it to him. You may leave this blank.
guide.editedHere: Your words for this step, as you changed them, are all here.
guide.editedFirst: Your words for this step, as you changed them, are all in its first question.
guide.reviewHint: Read it slowly, as if you are speaking to him. Change any words that are not true or do not sound like you, and join any words that run together.

welcome.heading: Teach Us to Pray
body: Each step shows the words of Jesus and asks you a question.
You answer in your own words. The app never writes a prayer for you.
welcome.choose: How would you like to pray?
welcome.byMyselfHint: A guided prayer in your own words. About 10 minutes.
welcome.shareHint: Guide someone who is ready to turn to Jesus as they pray in their own words.

step.moreLink: More from Scripture for this step

guided.q: Jesus called God his Father in heaven. Speak to him now. How will you begin?
cues: how you are coming to him today

guided.q: Tell him what you honor about him today.
Thank him for something from the last day or two.
Where in your life today do you want his will done? Tell him.
If there is a decision in front of you, ask him for his will in it.
Ask him plainly for what you need today.
Ask him for what someone else needs today. Say their name.
Tell him what you need forgiveness for.
If there is someone you need to forgive, tell him, and say their name.

steps.name: Keep us and deliver us
steps.note: The World English Bible prints one more sentence in this verse, with a footnote that some Greek texts omit it. It is not shown here.

guided.q: Tell him where you are being tempted right now.
cues: when I am tired or angry

guided.q: Ask him to deliver you from what you need delivering from.
Close your prayer to him in your own words.

share.name: Share Jesus

start.name: Before you begin
start.note: This is a conversation, not a script. The Father draws people to Jesus, so there is no need to push. Sit where you can both see the screen. Read each passage together, ask each question gently, listen, and type what they say in their own words. They may stop at any time.
start.ask: Do you understand what you are about to say to God?

cost.name: Count the cost
cost.extraNote: Jesus said this to prepare people, not to discourage them.
cost.ask: Jesus told people this at the start. Do you want to keep going?

notToday.heading: That is all right.
notToday.note: No one should be rushed. Thank them, stay their friend, and keep praying for them.

share.hint: Type what they say, in their own words. You may leave this blank.

guided.q: Speak to the Father now. Tell him, in your own words, who you believe Jesus is.
cues: God raised him from the dead

guided.q: Tell him honestly what you have done wrong, or how you have lived without him, that you want to turn from.
If you are ready to turn from that and follow Jesus, tell him so in your own words.
Ask him for what you need as you begin to follow him.

borrow.name: Words to borrow
borrow.note: These are prayers from Scripture. Use any of them as your own.

review.heading: Read it through together
review.hint: Read it slowly, as if you are speaking to him. Change any words that are not true or do not sound like them, and join any words that run together.
review.lineHint: To make a phrase shorter, start a new line.
review.empty: There are no words to pray yet.

walk.leaderLine: Read this phrase, then let them repeat it.

prayer.heading: Their prayer
prayer.intro: The prayer in their own words.

after.heading: After the prayer

sections.heading: Grace, not the words
sections.note: What matters is Jesus, not the exact words.

next.text: Read the Gospel of John, and pray each day.
When it gets hard, tell the person who prayed with you.

after.leaderNote: Follow up with them within a few days.

about.heading: About and privacy
who: This app exists only to serve the ministry of Jesus, the Son of God. It shows how he taught us to pray, so that you can pray in your own words. It helps a believer guide someone who is ready to turn to Jesus to pray in their own words. And it lets anyone read and study the whole Bible at their own pace.
It is free. There are no ads, no accounts, no donations and no tracking.
privacy: The app never sends anything about you. It has no accounts, cookies or analytics, and it uses no other website. The only things it downloads are its own files, including each book of the Bible the first time you open it, and each book's cross-references the first time you open them, from the same place the app comes from.
The website that hosts the app can see which books and cross-reference files are opened, as with any website. It cannot see your notes or prayers.

Your words leave the app only if you choose to send them yourself. "Copy" puts them on your clipboard. "Share" hands them to the app you pick on your own device. "Save as a file" puts a text file in your downloads. "Print" sends them to your printer.

Your prayer words are not kept after you close the app unless you turn on "Keep my draft on this device". If you do, your words are stored only in this browser, and "Erase my words" removes them. Erasing does not remove files you saved or copies you shared.

While you pray by yourself, your words are also kept for this visit only, in this browser tab, so that they are not lost if you open a chapter of the Bible or your phone closes the tab in the background. They are erased when you close the tab. Nothing is kept beyond the visit unless you turn on "Keep my draft on this device". Words typed in "Share Jesus" are never stored.

Bible study remembers the last chapter you read and a few display choices, such as hiding the translators' notes, on this device only, so you can carry on where you left off. Books you open are kept on this device so you can read them offline. Neither is ever sent anywhere.

My study keeps your notes and bookmarks in this browser on this device only, and only because you wrote them. They are never sent anywhere. A backup file contains your notes as readable text, so take care where you send it.

While you write a note, it is kept for this visit only, in this browser tab, so that it is not lost if your phone closes the tab in the background. It is erased when you save or cancel the note, or close the tab.
sources: The structure follows the prayer Jesus taught in Matthew 6:5-15 and Luke 11:1-4. Every other quotation is Scripture, shown with its reference.

Scripture quotations are from the World English Bible (WEB), which is in the public domain. The text was taken from eBible.org, from its files dated 21 November 2026. "World English Bible" is a trademark of eBible.org.
Where a reference ends in "a" or "b", only that part of the verse is shown. The words shown are unchanged.
Where an excerpt begins or ends partway through a speech, the quotation mark that opens or closes that speech elsewhere is not shown at the start or end of the excerpt.

The app adds no teaching of its own. The only words that are ours are the step names, headings and buttons, the questions, the short "Think about" prompts under them, the start screen, the instruction on the read-through screen, the reminders to pray out loud, and this page. In "Share Jesus", the leader notes, the questions and ideas, the instructions on the read-through and phrase screens, and the next steps are ours too. In Bible study, the headings, buttons and the short lines under the Apocrypha shelf are ours, and so are the labels and buttons in My study and the labels around the cross-references.

The text, book names and translators' notes in Bible study come from the same eBible.org files, by code, unchanged. Whole chapters are shown exactly as published. The translators' notes are marked as theirs and are not Scripture. The WEB's preface and glossary are not included.

Cross-references are from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge, in the CrossWire Bible Society's edition (version 1.4) dated about 1880, compiled from the work of Canne, Browne, Blayney, Scott and others. It is in the public domain. Its headings are in the words of the King James Version. A reference that does not match a verse in the WEB is shown as plain text. One exception: the TSK's references to Romans 16:25-27 open Romans 14:24-26, where the WEB prints those verses, as the WEB's own note says.
about.doxology: The World English Bible prints one more sentence at the end of Matthew 6:13, with a footnote that some Greek texts omit it. The guided prayer does not show that sentence. Bible study shows Matthew 6 exactly as the WEB publishes it, with that footnote.
about.license: The code is released under the MIT License. The Scripture text and the cross-references are in the public domain.
about.installHeading: Add the app to your home screen
install: The app can sit on your home screen like any other app. It then opens in one tap, works offline, and your phone is less likely to erase your notes and bookmarks.
iPhone or iPad (Safari): tap the Share button (a square with an arrow pointing up), then "Add to Home Screen", then "Add".
Android (Chrome): tap the menu (three dots at the top right), then "Add to Home screen" or "Install app", then confirm.
Computer (Chrome or Edge): click the install button at the right of the address bar, or open the browser menu and choose to install the app.
On iPhone and iPad, the app on your home screen keeps its own notes and bookmarks, separate from Safari. To move them across, save a backup file in Safari and open it in the app on your home screen.

You can keep your own complete copy of the app on each device. Open "Use offline" at the bottom of any page and tap "Keep everything on this device". The prayer guides, Share Jesus, the whole Bible and the cross-references then all work with no connection. Each device keeps its own copy, and nothing is shared between them.
how: There are seven steps, in the order Jesus gave. Each step shows his words and asks you one short question at a time. Most questions show a short prayer from Scripture, and each step offers other passages of Scripture that change each day.
Before you pray, you read your whole prayer through in one place and change anything that is not true or does not sound like you. Then you pray it out loud, one part at a time.
At the end you see your prayer in your own words. The app never writes a prayer for you, and it never changes your words.

"Share Jesus" helps a believer guide someone who is ready to turn to Jesus. It shows Scripture, asks a few questions, and ends with a prayer in that person's own words, said aloud phrase by phrase. The app never writes the prayer, never says that saying it saves anyone, and never keeps their words on the device.

Bible study has the whole World English Bible, with the Apocrypha on its own shelf. You can go to any chapter, search, and read offline. Each chapter has its own link, so you can open the same place on another device.

My study lets you bookmark verses in six colours you can name, write notes that link to passages and to each other, and save a backup file. Under any verse in the 66 books, you can open cross-references from the Treasury of Scripture Knowledge.
